summary: Implements random-access reads over remote objects for read_stream(access='random'). RangePolicy is a frozen, validated cache policy (readahead, blockcache, bytes or none; block_size; max_blocks) with from_profile() resolving per-field RANGE_* profile settings against library defaults. RangedSource is a backend-supplied description of one object (size, a half-open range fetch callable, optional on_close). RangedReader is a seekable io.RawIOBase that serves reads through an fsspec cache, performs no I/O on seek, and rejects short range responses.
key_classes: RangePolicy(cache='readahead', block_size=1 MiB, max_blocks=32) — frozen, validated range-cache policy; public
RangedSource(size, fetch, on_close=None) — backend-to-reader contract for one object; returned by RangedReadProtocol implementations
RangedReader(source, policy) — seekable RawIOBase over an fsspec cache; owns source.on_close
key_functions: RangePolicy.from_profile(profile) -> RangePolicy — build a policy from a profile's RANGE_CACHE/RANGE_BLOCK_SIZE/RANGE_MAX_BLOCKS, each overriding defaults individually
strong_etag(value) -> str | None — return the ETag only if it is strong (not W/), for If-Match pinning
extension_points: A backend gains random-access support by implementing RangedReadProtocol and returning a RangedSource (size + fetch(start, end) + optional on_close); the facade wraps it in RangedReader
Cache strategies are the fsspec caches registry entries named by RangePolicy.cache
lifecycle_notes: fsspec is imported inside RangedReader.__init__, so the module imports on a base install; constructing a reader needs the [http] stack
Precedence: caller range_policy replaces the profile policy entirely; otherwise profile RANGE_* fields override defaults field by field (docs/read-access-modes.md)
RangedReader.close() calls source.on_close once, then drops the cache; repeated close is a no-op
Handles are not safe for concurrent seek/read
documentation_hooks: docs/read-access-modes.md: random mode, cache policies, precedence and Parquet tuning table
Backend author guide: implementing RangedReadProtocol and RangedSource
Consistency note: strong ETags pinned with If-Match, weak/missing ETags give no guarantee
risks: RangedReader.read calls self._cache._fetch, a private fsspec API; an fsspec release that renames it breaks random mode
A large caller read(n) allocates n bytes; cache settings do not bound result size (documented)
max_blocks is silently ignored for caches other than blockcache
No runnable example in examples/ covers random access; the only usage samples are in docs/read-access-modes.md

evidence.detail: facade constructs RangedReader(source, policy) with range_policy or RangePolicy.from_profile
documents RangePolicy defaults, caches, precedence and error behaviour
